records.summary: The records show 737 Irving St has operated as a restaurant continuously since at least 2003. The site history includes six Planning Department approvals between 2003-2020, all for restaurant use including multiple ABC Type 47 (full bar) licenses and a 2020 limited restaurant approval. A restaurant use is principally permitted in the NCD-Inner Sunset zoning district on the first story (Planning Code § 730). The block is extremely dense with 43 registered food and drink businesses within 500 feet, including 4 bars and 19 active ABC on-sale licenses within that radius. The Inner Sunset has seen very light use-decision activity over the past 5 years—only 5 dated decisions within 1,000 feet, too few to establish an approval rate, though 2 were approved outright and 3 approved with conditions.

comparables.why_comparable: Same address (737 Irving St), same NCD-Inner Sunset zoning, restaurant use approved in November 2020. This is the most recent Planning decision for the subject property itself.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral for a limited restaurant at 737 Irving was approved in 25 days without conditions, confirming restaurant use is permitted at this address under continuation of established use.

comparables.why_comparable: Formula retail limited-restaurant (Yi Fang Taiwan Fruit Tea) approved 83 meters away at 645 Irving St in the same NCD-Inner Sunset district. Required a Conditional Use Authorization hearing for the formula retail component.
comparables.key_takeaway: Formula retail restaurant required a CUA and took 279 days from filing to approval, but was approved with only standard eating-and-drinking conditions (sidewalk maintenance, noise, odor, trash, community liaison). No special restrictions on formula retail restaurants in this district.

comparables.why_comparable: Immediately adjacent at 731 Irving St (10 meters), same block, same NCD-Inner Sunset zoning. Restaurant continuation approved without conditions.
comparables.key_takeaway: Restaurant use approved next door as continuation of existing use (Villa Romana to Lale), confirming the corridor's established restaurant character and that continuation approvals are routine in this location.

comparables.why_comparable: Multi-location chain restaurant (Pluto's, 7 locations) approved at 627 Irving St, 106 meters away in NCD-Inner Sunset. Agency referral for ABC Type 41 with explicit finding that Pluto's is not formula retail.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning found that a 7-location chain was not formula retail in the Inner Sunset NCD; Super Duper's 11 locations may trigger formula retail review, but the district allows formula retail restaurants without additional authorization beyond standard CUA process.

comparables.why_comparable: Non-formula restaurant at 627 Irving St (106 meters) approved for ABC Type 41, same NCD-Inner Sunset zoning, decided in 6 days as agency referral.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral approvals for restaurant use in this district are routine and fast (under one week), though these are continuations rather than new uses requiring hearings.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant ABC Type 41 referral at 1378 9th Ave (137 meters), NCD-Inner Sunset, approved in 5 days. Notes that formula retail is not permitted but restaurant use is per Planning Code Section 730.
comparables.key_takeaway: Agency referral explicitly states formula retail not permitted, but this refers to over-the-counter approvals; formula retail restaurants still require CUA process as shown by the Yi Fang approval.

comparables.why_comparable: Change of use from limited restaurant to full restaurant at 1239 9th Ave (167 meters) in NCD-Inner Sunset, approved via CUA in 78 days with no extracted conditions.
comparables.key_takeaway: CUA for restaurant intensification (limited to full) approved within 3 months without special conditions, showing the Commission's receptiveness to restaurant uses on this corridor.

comparables.why_comparable: Restaurant at 1330 9th Ave (46 meters) seeking ABC Type 41, approved as continuation of existing use under Planning Code Section 178(b), which allows existing uses to remain.
comparables.key_takeaway: Planning Code Section 178(b) continuation-of-use provisions are routinely invoked in this district for spaces with prior restaurant history, potentially applicable to 737 Irving given its continuous restaurant use since at least 2003.

patterns.pattern: Restaurant uses in the NCD-Inner Sunset are principally permitted on the first story and routinely approved as continuations of existing use under Planning Code Section 178(b) when the space has prior restaurant history.

Formula retail restaurants in NCD-Inner Sunset require Conditional Use Authorization and a Commission hearing, but are approved with only standard eating-and-drinking conditions (sidewalk/trash maintenance, noise, odor control, community liaison).
Agency referrals (DPH, ABC) for restaurant use at established restaurant locations in this district are approved in 5–30 days without conditions when the use is a continuation.

Multi-location chains operating in the district have been approved; a 7-location chain (Pluto's) was found not to be formula retail, but an 11-location concept will likely require formula retail CUA review.

The Irving Street corridor between 7th and 10th Avenues shows consistent approval of restaurant uses with no denials or withdrawals in the candidate set, reflecting the corridor's established dining character.

Standard conditions for approved eating-and-drinking uses include sidewalk maintenance within one-block radius, soundproofing, odor control, trash concealment, community liaison appointment, and monitoring fees.

risk.concept_summary: Super Duper Burgers proposes a 2,231 sq ft fast-casual burger restaurant with full cooking, background music, exterior signage and tenant improvements at 737 Irving St in the NCD-Inner Sunset district.

overall.next_step: File a Conditional Use Authorization application with San Francisco Planning for the formula retail component (11 locations), including a pre-application meeting and neighborhood outreach plan, before signing the lease or committing to construction.

approvals.summary: Formula retail requires a Conditional Use Authorization hearing because the chain operates 11 locations; restaurant use itself is principally permitted in the NCD-Inner Sunset district on the first story.

findings.text: A restaurant use on the first story is principally permitted in the NCD-Inner Sunset zoning district under Planning Code § 730.
Formula retail uses require Conditional Use Authorization in the NCD-Inner Sunset district under Planning Code § 730.

The space at 737 Irving St has operated continuously as a restaurant since at least 2003, with six Planning approvals on file including multiple ABC Type 47 full-bar licenses through 2010 and a limited restaurant approval in November 2020.

A formula retail limited-restaurant (Yi Fang Taiwan Fruit Tea) at 645 Irving St, 83 meters away in the same district, was approved via CUA in February 2020 after 279 days, with only standard eating-and-drinking conditions (sidewalk maintenance, noise, odor control, trash, community liaison).

Within 1,000 feet in the NCD-Inner Sunset district, N=5 dated use decisions over the past 5 years show 2 approved and 3 approved with conditions; no denials or withdrawals, but too few cases for a rate.

Whether the space was last used as a laundromat is not established; if it was, Planning Code § 202.12 (in force from December 2021 to December 2024) would have required a Conditional Use for change of use or demolition, but that ordinance expired before this report date.

approvals.summary: Health permit to operate is issued after plan check and pre-opening inspection without a hearing, and the DPH application will be referred to Planning for zoning review.

findings.text: A restaurant with a full kitchen requires a health permit to operate, issued by SF Department of Public Health after plan check, equipment approval and final inspection.
The most recent DPH referral at 737 Irving St (2020-010191MIS) for a limited restaurant was approved by Planning in 25 days.
DPH health permit applications for restaurants are referred to the Planning Department for zoning review under the interagency referral process.

findings.text: No active ABC license is on file at 737 Irving St, so the records do not show the current use of the space.
The description does not state what the space was last used as, so whether the proposed restaurant is a Planning Code change of use is not established.

A restaurant or bar is Building Code occupancy Group A-2, but a space for fewer than 50 people is Group B; the description does not give occupancy load, so the proposed occupancy group is not established.
The existing occupancy group is not in public records and can only be determined from plans or an inspection, so whether a change of occupancy is required is not established.
Building permits with a change of use are routed to Planning for zoning review and neighborhood notification where required under Planning Code § 175.

expected_conditions.condition: Sidewalk maintenance: maintain the main entrance and all abutting sidewalks in a clean condition, and monitor the sidewalk within one-block radius during business hours to keep it free of litter associated with the business.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition for eating-and-drinking uses in the Yi Fang CUA at 645 Irving St and typical of all San Francisco restaurant approvals under Article 1, Section 34 of the Police Code and DPW Street and Sidewalk Maintenance Standards.

expected_conditions.condition: Noise control: the premises shall be adequately soundproofed so that incidental noise is not audible beyond the premises, and fixed-source equipment noise shall not exceed the decibel levels in the SF Noise Control Ordinance.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the Yi Fang CUA and typical for all eating-and-drinking uses in enclosed spaces to protect adjacent residents.

expected_conditions.condition: Odor control: appropriate odor control equipment shall be installed and maintained to prevent noxious or offensive odors from escaping the premises.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the Yi Fang CUA and typical for restaurants with full cooking to address complaints from nearby residents.

expected_conditions.condition: Trash concealment: garbage, recycling and compost containers shall be kept within the premises and hidden from public view, and placed outside only when being serviced by the disposal company.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the Yi Fang CUA and required under DPW garbage and recycling receptacles guidelines.

expected_conditions.condition: Community liaison: appoint a community liaison officer to deal with issues of concern to owners and occupants of nearby properties, and provide the Zoning Administrator and neighborhood groups with the liaison's contact information.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in the Yi Fang CUA and typical for CUA approvals to ensure ongoing communication with the neighborhood.

expected_conditions.condition: Validity and diligent pursuit: the authorization is valid for three years; a building or site permit must be issued within that period, and construction must commence and proceed diligently to completion.
expected_conditions.basis: Standard condition in all CUA approvals to prevent approvals from lapsing without implementation.

filing_playbook.action: Request a pre-application meeting with SF Planning Department to confirm formula retail determination and discuss continuation-of-use under § 178(b) given the space's continuous restaurant history.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that Super Duper Burgers operates 11 locations and seeks to occupy 737 Irving St, which has operated as a restaurant continuously since at least 2003 with six prior Planning approvals. Ask whether the application will be treated as a new formula retail use requiring full CUA or whether continuation-of-use provisions apply. Request guidance on neighborhood outreach, environmental review and hearing timeline. Bring site history records and the 2020 limited restaurant approval.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State and obtain an EIN from the IRS.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC) or Articles of Incorporation online at the CA Secretary of State bizfile portal, then apply for an EIN at irs.gov the same day. The entity name and EIN are required for the business registration, seller's permit, lease and all city permits.

filing_playbook.action: Register the business with SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector to obtain a Business Account Number (BAN).
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the business registration application online with the entity name, EIN, address, gross receipts projection and business activities. The BAN is required for all other SF permits. Tiered fee is $55–$700 depending on projected gross receipts.

filing_playbook.action: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning Department for the formula retail component, including neighborhood outreach plan and project description.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: State that Super Duper Burgers operates 11 locations and proposes a 2,231 sq ft fast-casual restaurant at 737 Irving St with full cooking, seating, background music and exterior signage. Emphasize the space's continuous restaurant use since 2003 and compatibility with the neighborhood's dining character. Commit to standard operating conditions: sidewalk maintenance, noise and odor control, trash concealment, community liaison. Schedule the pre-application community meeting and post the required notice at the site for 30 days. Request First Year Free fee waiver if eligible as a new storefront business.

filing_playbook.action: Submit DPH plan check application for the kitchen build-out with scaled drawings, equipment list, menu and finishes schedule.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File online through the DPH portal with the BAN, Location ID and EIN. Submit two sets of scaled drawings showing the kitchen layout, equipment, hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, mop sink, finishes and ventilation. Include the menu and a list of all food-contact equipment. State that the concept is a fast-casual burger restaurant with grills, fryers, hood and walk-in cooler. Budget $2,207 plan-check fee (8 hours, new restaurant) and allow 21–60 days for review. Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction complete.

filing_playbook.action: Engage an architect to prepare building permit drawings for the tenant improvements, including the kitchen, hood, restrooms, ADA upgrades and any change of occupancy.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Provide the architect with the lease, site survey, existing conditions and the project scope: full kitchen build-out, grease hood, walk-in cooler, ADA restrooms, hand sinks, finishes and signage. Ask the architect to determine the occupancy group (A-2 if 50+ people, B if fewer) and whether a change of occupancy is required. Coordinate the building permit routing with DPH plan check so both are reviewed in parallel. The architect will also prepare the FOG interceptor sizing and SFFD hood suppression plans.

filing_playbook.action: File the building permit application with DBI once the CUA is approved, with plans stamped by the architect and routed to Planning, DPH, SFFD and SFPUC.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit the complete plan set with the BAN, property address and CUA Motion number. Include architectural, mechanical, electrical and plumbing sheets. Route the permit to Planning (zoning review), DPH (health plan check), SFFD (hood suppression and place of assembly if 50+ occupancy) and SFPUC (FOG interceptor). State that the project is tenant improvements for a restaurant with full cooking, and that the CUA for formula retail has been approved. Budget $800–$15,000 in permit fees (percentage of construction valuation) and 14–120 days for review. Licensed contractors will pull separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits.

filing_playbook.action: After DPH plan check approval and construction is substantially complete, schedule the DPH pre-opening inspection and apply for the health permit to operate.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Book the pre-opening inspection with the DPH plan reviewer at least two weeks in advance. Ensure the kitchen is fully built per approved plans: all equipment installed, hand sinks operational, hot water at 120°F, walls and floors sealed, trash enclosure ready. Have a certified food safety manager on staff (ServSafe or equivalent). Submit the health permit application online with the BAN, Location ID, EIN and proof of the food safety certification. The inspector will verify compliance and issue the permit. Budget $470 application fee (includes initial inspection) and $0 annual license fee for 2026–28.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost cover the Conditional Use Authorization for formula retail and the health permit to operate, the two approvals in the entitlement path. The CUA takes 120–300 days from filing to approval when granted, including pre-application meeting, application preparation, environmental review, 30-day posted notice, Commission hearing and 30-day appeal period. The Yi Fang formula retail restaurant CUA at 645 Irving St took 279 days. The health permit is issued 14–45 days after plan check approval and final inspection. Government costs: CUA application estimated $3,100 (2026–27 CPI-adjusted, no construction), health plan check $2,207 (new restaurant, 8 hours), health permit application $470, business registration $55–$700 (tiered by gross receipts). These figures exclude the building permit (insufficient information to establish whether it is required), architect and contractor fees, and pre-CUA costs (entity formation $70–$150, EIN $0, seller's permit $0). The timeline is to approval; it is not a time to denial or withdrawal.
